candidate_additions: Sult2a8 specifically called out as the major mouse liver 7α-OH bile acid sulfotransferase (sharper gene-function assignment)
New Psmd1 proteasome-mediated mechanism regulating hepatocellular lipid droplet accumulation via p38-JNK/AKT signaling
Aldh1a1 connected to NAFLD-relevant vitamin A/retinaldehyde metabolism
Cdo1 linked to coenzyme A synthesis balance as an added downstream consequence
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Nrf2/CAR nuclear receptor transcriptional coordination of the Phase I/II detox module (including CAR-Mrp4 cholestasis-protective link) is dropped from mechanism 1
Cyp2c50, a cytochrome P450 (phase I) gene, is removed entirely from the candidate's mechanistic coverage
Eci2 (unsaturated fatty acid beta-oxidation) and Lonp2 (peroxisomal protein quality control) are dropped from the fatty acid oxidation mechanism
Agmat (agmatinase, urea/polyamine pathway) is dropped from the sulfur/nitrogen mechanism
The specific Cdo1-to-gluconeogenesis mechanistic claim (CDO1 knockdown raises liver cysteine and glucose output, PMID 39819116) is dropped
decision_relevant_differences: Loss of the Nrf2/CAR regulatory framing changes how upstream transcriptional control of the detox module would be interpreted
Dropping Cyp2c50 shifts mechanism 1 from a combined phase I/II oxidative-and-conjugative program to a purely phase II sulfation/conjugation program
Addition of Psmd1 introduces a distinct post-translational (proteasome-mediated) regulatory route for lipid droplet accumulation not present in the baseline
Removing the Cdo1-gluconeogenesis link changes the claimed physiological consequence of Cdo1 activity from glucose output control to CoA synthesis balance
assessment.rationale: Both annotations converge on the same three-theme architecture (Phase II bile acid/steroid sulfation, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation/lipid droplet handling, sulfur/nitrogen catabolism with an aging signature) and rely on largely overlapping gene sets and regulators, so the core biological identity of P25 is unchanged. However, the candidate drops the baseline's explicit Nrf2/CAR transcriptional-regulation narrative and the Cyp2c50 phase I enzyme, swaps Eci2/Lonp2 for a new Psmd1 proteasome-lipogenesis mechanism, and replaces the cited Cdo1-gluconeogenesis link with a CoA-synthesis claim. These are meaningful gene-function and mechanistic refinements/losses rather than a wholesale reinterpretation, placing this at same_core_with_meaningful_refinement with mixed evidence depth change (gains in some gene-specific detail, losses in regulatory/mechanistic specificity elsewhere).
shared_core_conclusions: Program organizes into three themes: bile acid/hydroxysteroid Phase II sulfation, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation with lipid droplet handling, and sulfur amino acid catabolism/metabolic aging
SULT2A family (Sult2a5/7/8) plus Gsta3/Akr1c6/Aldh1a1 drive Phase II detoxification of bile acids and steroids
Hao2, Aldh3a2, Fitm1 (and Cyb5b) support peroxisomal/microsomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid aldehyde/triglyceride handling
Cdo1 is the rate-limiting, bile acid/FXR-regulated cysteine dioxygenase feeding taurine and GSH synthesis
Rgn/SMP30 marks hepatocyte aging decline; Car5a and Alad extend the program into urea cycle/heme synthesis support
Regulators Insig1, Abcg5, G6pc, Dgat2 tie the program to hepatic lipid/sterol/glucose homeostasis and MASLD relevance
